title: Late Fee Relief for Hospital and Rehabilitation Absences (Assisted Living)
content:
Under the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement, a hospital or rehabilitation-facility absence during the billing month relieves the late fee. The absence is the one recorded on the residency, with its reason, start date and return date; the billing month is the month the late fee is assessed for.

**Relief midnights.** The relief midnights are counted, in calendar days, from the later of the absence start date and the first day of the billing month to the earlier of the absence return date and the last day of the billing month; an absence wholly outside the billing month gives none. An absence whose reason is a family visit gives no relief midnights.

| Relief midnights in the billing month | The late fee is multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 15 or more | 0.5 |
| 1 to 14 (one to fewer than 15) | 0.75 |
| None | Unchanged |

The multiplication acts on the whole late fee before it is rounded once to the cent.

### Questions answered (billing month of March; hypothetical absences)

**A hospital stay from 20 February to 10 March?** Counted from 1 March to 10 March: 9 relief midnights, so 0.75.

**A rehabilitation-facility stay from 10 March to 25 March?** 15 relief midnights, so 0.5; had the return been on 24 March, 14 relief midnights and 0.75.

**A hospital stay from 28 March to 15 April?** Counted from 28 March to 31 March: 3 relief midnights, so 0.75.

**A family visit from 1 March to 31 March?** No relief midnights; the late fee is unchanged.

Illustration: a late fee of 111.36 with 9 relief midnights becomes 111.36 multiplied by 0.75, that is 83.52.
